# Results — Study 354 (The Wheel)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The retail "Wheel" — sell a
cash-secured ATM **put** each month; if assigned, sell ATM covered **calls**; repeat for
"income" — tested on a real SPY tape. We price each month's one-month ATM option with
**Black-Scholes**, using **VIX/100 as the implied vol** (a transparent, clearly-labelled
model — no live option chain), and simulate the Wheel against buy-and-hold SPY and a cash
baseline. Deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` (`--fetch` once to download the
SPY+VIX cache) to reproduce every number below.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | SPY total-return adjusted close + ^VIX level (yfinance, public, no key) |
| As-of (last bar) | **2026-06-18** (the stamped sample drops the in-progress June 2026 month) |
| Window | 1993-01-31 → 2026-05-31 · **401** month-end observations |
| Premium model | one-month ATM Black-Scholes, IV = VIX/100, r = 0 (so call = put = 2Φ(σ√t/2)−1) |
| SPY level range | $24.11 – $754.54 · VIX mean **19.6%** / median 17.9% · avg premium kept **2.25%/mo** |

> **Model caveats (named on the axes).** *(1) VIX-as-IV is a transparent proxy, not a live
> chain.* It is on average **above** SPY's realised vol (19.6% implied vs ~14.9% realised) —
> the **variance risk premium** — so the model *flatters the option seller*; any shortfall the
> Wheel shows is conservative, and any edge it shows is the VRP, not a free lunch. *(2) No early
> assignment, fixed monthly ATM strikes, no skew/term-structure, European exercise, frictionless
> roll.* These simplifications make the Wheel **look better** than a real chain would (American
> puts, bid/ask, slippage, pin risk). *(3) One 33-year US-equity regime.* The edge is regime-
> conditioned — see the half-sample split.

## The decomposition — the Wheel is the option payoff (positive control)

Holding cash-or-ETF with one short ATM option, the Wheel's monthly P&L is an **identity**, not
a fitted effect: *capped move on the side you are short* **+** *premium kept*. The synthetic
control prices the option at the world's **own** volatility and confirms it:

| world | edge over buy-and-hold (ann) | t | up-capture | down-capture | Wheel skew |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| fair IV, no crashes | **−3.71%** | −7.9 | 45% | 46% | −1.67 |
| fair IV, 1%/mo crashes | −3.37% | −7.2 | 45% | 51% | −3.00 |
| IV = 1.2× realised (a VRP), 1%/mo crashes | +1.05% | +2.3 | 55% | 42% | −3.00 |

At a **fair** price the Wheel **loses** to buy-and-hold by ~3.7%/yr — it surrenders the index's
drift-driven upside (up-capture ~45%) and keeps a symmetric premium. It only turns positive when
you *assume* the implied vol sits above realised (the VRP). **The Wheel has no edge of its own;
its only possible edge is the variance risk premium.** The Black-Scholes engine matches the
closed form exactly (call = put = 2Φ(σ√t/2)−1 to machine precision).

## Half 1 — the Wheel vs buy-and-hold on the real tape

| series | CAGR | vol | Sharpe | max drawdown | skew | $1 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Wheel** (VIX-priced) | **11.61%** | 8.7% | **1.32** | −22.8% | **−1.87** | 39.2× |
| Buy-and-hold SPY | 8.09% | 14.9% | 0.60 | −55.8% | −0.36 | 13.4× |
| Cash @ 3%/yr | 3.04% | — | — | — | — | 2.7× |

Gross of costs the VIX-priced Wheel beats buy-and-hold on CAGR **and** Sharpe — because VIX
ran ~5 vol-points rich of realised for 33 years (the VRP the model bakes in). But the
**advantage is not robust**, and it is the *opposite* of "market-neutral income": skew **−1.87**
(vs SPY's −0.36) is the short-vol fingerprint.

## Half 2 — the "income" edge is WEAK / MIXED (it flips sign by regime)

Paired *t* of the Wheel's **monthly excess return over buy-and-hold** (the Signal axis):

| sample | edge (ann) | paired t | n | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **full 1993–2026** | **+2.50%** | **+1.73** | 401 | below the t = 2 bar |
| first half 1993–2009 | +6.21% | +3.11 | 200 | high-VIX / crisis-rich era |
| second half 2009–2026 | **−1.20%** | **−0.58** | 201 | the Wheel **trails** the index |

The edge **flips sign** across halves: strongly positive when VIX was rich and crises frequent
(1993–2009), **negative** through the post-2010 bull market when the surrendered upside swamped
the premium. A sign-flipping effect that does not clear t = 2 on the full sample is **MIXED /
WEAK**, not a real, harvestable "income" edge.

## Half 3 — the short-vol shape (truncated upside, near-full downside)

| | SPY mean | Wheel mean | capture |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| up months (n = 253) | +3.24% | +2.25% | **69%** |
| down months (n = 147) | −3.55% | −1.28% | **36%** |

The VRP-rich premium cushions the *down* months here (36% capture), but the **up** months are
truncated to 69% — and in the worst events the Wheel still bleeds: worst single month **−12.3%**
(March 2020), 2008 **−10.7%**, and the worst 5 Wheel months sum to **−51%**. This is short
volatility in a costume: a directional long-equity position that gives away the right tail and
keeps the left.

## Tradability — the gross edge dies to costs

Cost sweep (one-way cost per option written; assignment/roll turnover):

| one-way cost / option | edge over B&H (ann) | paired t | Wheel CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00% | +2.50% | +1.73 | 11.61% |
| 0.10% | +1.30% | +0.90 | 10.29% |
| **0.25%** | **−0.50%** | **−0.35** | 8.33% |
| 0.50% | −3.50% | −2.43 | 5.15% |

A realistic retail option spread of ~25 bp per write **flips the edge negative**. With a
−1.87 skew, a fat left tail (worst-5 = −51%), an edge that already sign-flipped by regime, and
no cushion once costs bite, the Wheel is **FRAGILE** — survivable only sized small and
crash-aware, not a money machine.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The "income beats the index" edge flips sign by regime (+6.2%/yr,
  t = 3.1 in 1993–2009; **−1.2%/yr, t = −0.6** since 2010), with a full-sample t = **1.73**
  below the bar. At a **fair** implied vol the control shows the Wheel *loses* to buy-and-hold
  by ~3.7%/yr — its only possible edge is the variance risk premium, not the wheel mechanic.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Great gross Sharpe (**1.32** vs 0.60) but the edge dies at
  ~**25 bp**/option of cost (t → −0.35) and the payoff carries skew **−1.87**, a −22.8% drawdown
  even in this generous model, and worst-5 months of −51%. One crash hurts; harvestable only
  sized and disciplined.
- **"Free / market-neutral income"? — BUSTED.** The Wheel keeps **69%** of up months and only
  cushions to **36%** of down months — a directional long-beta position with truncated upside,
  skew −1.87. It is a packaged short-volatility / covered-call exposure (cf. Study 62
  premium-seller, Study 63 free-fall), not income, and certainly not market-neutral.
